# flat

<link-summary>Flattens a nested object into one level of dotted keys.</link-summary>

<web-summary>flat() — Flattens a nested object into one level of dotted keys. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/object</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function flat(source: object, depth: number = Infinity): Record<string, unknown>;
```

Nested objects become dotted paths; arrays are kept whole, because their indices are data rather than structure. `depth` stops the descent — `1` flattens the first level only.

The inverse walk is `getPath`, which reads a value back out by the same kind of path.

## Parameters

| Parameter                         | Type     | Description                                                         |
| :-------------------------------- | :------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `source`                          | `object` | The object to flatten. It must not be an array.                     |
| `depth` _(optional)_ `= Infinity` | `number` | How many levels to descend. Any whole number; unlimited by default. |

## Returns

`Record<string, unknown>` — a new flat object keyed by dotted paths.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                   |
| :------------------------- | :-------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not an object. |

## Examples

### Flattening

```javascript
flat({ a: { b: 1 }, c: [1, 2] }); // => { "a.b": 1, "c": [1, 2] }
flat({ a: { b: { c: 1 } } }, 1); // => { "a.b": { "c": 1 } }
```
